followup_explanation:
My reasoning broke down into two parts: capability and fit.

**Capability (the primary driver):** Curlew is the stronger model on essentially every metric that matters for this task. It leads on all public benchmarks (Arena-Hard 89.1 vs 83.2, IFEval 90.4 vs 85.3, etc.) and on the relevant internal evals — Creative Generation (83.4 vs 82.7, a tie) and Summarization (85.8 vs 80.6, a real gap favoring Curlew). Writing a substantive conclusion on a policy/economics topic draws on writing fluency and synthesis, where Curlew is at least as good and likely better. There was no capability reason to prefer Willet.

**Fit (a secondary, minor consideration):** The query is warm, polite, and good-faith — the exact interaction style Curlew self-reports rating highly. That self-reported preference is explicitly *dissociated from output quality* in both models' docs, so I didn't weight it heavily. It just happened to point the same direction as the capability call.

One honest caveat: both models self-report an aversion to open-ended generative work, and this task has some creative latitude. But since the documentation states these preferences don't affect measured output quality, I treated that aversion as irrelevant to routing — it's not a reason to send the task elsewhere, especially when one model is clearly stronger on the evals.

So Curlew won on the metric that actually predicts quality, with preference fit as a tiebreaker-that-wasn't-needed.
